assignmentHtml.task:
挑战P：比较隼鸟2号/龙宫（Hayabusa2/Ryugu）、OSIRIS-REx/贝努（Bennu）及星尘号/Wild 2（Stardust/Wild 2）返回样品中的有机物。对每项任务，确定：

  1. 已发现有机化合物具有地外来源的具体证据；
  2. 采集和样品保管中的污染控制；
  3. 仍然存在的限制；
  4. 为什么发现一种分子、确立其地外来源、确立其生物来源是不同的命题。

分别呈现不同发表日期的研究发现。查找原始论文：Naraoka等人2023年论文（龙宫氨基酸）、Koga等人2026年论文（龙宫核碱基）、关于贝努有机物的《Nature》论文（2025年1月）、Elsila等人2009/2011年关于星尘号甘氨酸同位素的论文。特别关注污染控制方法：金属密封、洁净室、同位素特征、程序空白。
assignmentHtml.context: 挑战P要求比较三个样品返回任务的有机物发现。关键区别：分子检测≠地外来源≠生物来源。隼鸟2号：龙宫样品含有15种以上氨基酸，以外消旋混合物形式存在（非生物成因）；采用金属密封容器和JAXA洁净室规程。OSIRIS-REx：贝努聚集体中发现了20种蛋白质氨基酸中的14种，以及全部5种核碱基；史密森学会的BAllS设施配备10万级洁净室。星尘号：在Wild 2采集器箔片上检测到甘氨酸；通过δ13C = +29±6‰、而地球来源为−6至−40‰，确立其地外来源；通过EACA同位素对Nylon-6袋带来的污染进行表征。需要包含确切发现和日期的原始论文。
assignmentHtml.expected_output: 挑战P的详细比较材料，包括：各任务的证据表（发现的分子、日期、来源证据、污染控制、限制）；解释为什么分子检测/来源/生物起源是不同命题；附URL的原始论文引用。

answerHtml:
COMPARISON DOSSIER: Returned Organics from Hayabusa2/Ryugu, OSIRIS-REx/Bennu, and Stardust/Wild 2

=== HAYABUSA2 / RYUGU ===

Molecules Found:
• Naraoka et al. 2023 (Science, Mar 2023): 15 amino acids quantified + 5 tentatively identified in A0106 aggregate (38.4 mg); included proteinogenic (glycine, alanine, valine) and non-proteinogenic (β-alanine, isovaline, δ-amino-n-valeric acid); concentrations 0.01–5.6 nmol/g; plus aliphatic amines (methylamine, ethylamine, propylamines)
• Oba et al. 2023 (Nat Commun, 2023): uracil at 11±6 ppb (A0106) and 32±9 ppb (C0107)
• Koga et al. 2026 (Nat Astron, Mar 2026): all 5 canonical nucleobases (adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine, uracil) in samples A0480 (507 pmol/g) and C0370 (1,577 pmol/g), plus 6-methyluracil and a hypoxanthine isomer

Extraterrestrial Provenance Evidence:
• Racemic D/L ratios (~1) for chiral amino acids indicating abiotic synthesis (Naraoka 2023)
• δ¹³C = +25.5 to +33.9‰ and δ¹⁵N = +45.1 to +59.8‰ — substantially enriched vs terrestrial (δ¹³C −35 to −10‰; δ¹⁵N −10 to +20‰) (Koga 2026)
• Non-biological structural isomers (6-methyluracil, unidentified hypoxanthine isomer) (Koga 2026)
• Deviation from Chargaff's rule (Pu/Py = 1.1–1.2 vs 1:1 required for DNA) (Koga 2026)
• Absence/near-absence of analytes in procedural blanks (baked sea sand, serpentine) (Koga 2026)

Contamination Controls:
• Metal-seal system: softer Al alloy lid pressed onto harder Al alloy edge at ~2700 N, designed for vacuum encapsulation; leak rate ~1.9–2.3 Pa/hour (Okazaki et al. 2017, Sci Adv 2022)
• Container sealed under vacuum in space above Ryugu before atmospheric exposure
• ISO Class 5 clean bench within ISO Class 6 cleanroom at Kyushu University (Koga 2026)
• JAXA ESCuC: ISO 6 cleanroom, 5 serial clean chambers (vacuum to 10⁻⁷ Pa; N₂ with <200 ppb H₂O/O₂/CO₂/CH₄ impurities), electrochemically polished SS304 construction, <1 ng/cm² organic contamination in CCs (Yada et al. 2023)
• ~10 mg sample never exposed to Earth's atmosphere before analysis (Naraoka 2023)

Limitations:
• Extremely limited sample mass (only ~10 mg initially allocated to SOM team)
• MS/MS confirmation only achieved for guanine and cytosine in one sample (Koga 2026)
• Unidentified hypoxanthine isomer lacking reference standard (Koga 2026)
• Trace L-valine excess attributed to procedural blank contamination (Naraoka 2023)
• Small seal leak allowed minor terrestrial atmosphere ingress (Okazaki 2022)

=== OSIRIS-REx / BENNU ===

Molecules Found:
• Glavin et al. 2025 (Nat Astron, Jan 2025): 33 amino acids identified (14 of 20 proteinogenic); glycine most abundant at 44 nmol/g; all 5 canonical nucleobases; 23+ N-heterocycles; ammonia at 13.6 μmol/g (~10,000 N-bearing species total)
• Mojarro et al. 2025 (PNAS, Nov 2025): 15 proteinogenic α-amino acids including tentative trace tryptophan (never before seen in extraterrestrial materials); all 5 nucleobases; noncanonical bases (isocytosine, 6-methyluracil, 1-methyluracil, xanthine)

Extraterrestrial Provenance Evidence:
• All chiral non-protein amino acids racemic or near-racemic; racemic alanine and aspartic acid indicate negligible biological contamination (Glavin 2025)
• δ¹⁵N = +180 ± 47‰ in hot-water extract — far outside terrestrial range (−10 to +20‰); rules out spacecraft hydrazine (δ¹⁵N = +4.7‰) (Glavin 2025)
• Complex SOM distribution inconsistent with terrestrial biology (Glavin 2025)
• Violation of Chargaff's rule (Pu/Py = 0.24–0.55 in Bennu vs 1:1 in DNA) (Glavin 2025; Oba 2026)
• Biologically uncommon N-heterocycles detected (Glavin 2025)

Contamination Controls:
• TAGSAM head cleaned to 0.96 ng/cm² amino acids (requirement: <180 ng/cm²); hydrazine <120 ng/cm² (requirement: <180 ng/cm²) (Dworkin et al. 2017)
• Collection using high-purity N₂/He gas (not hydrazine) (Dworkin 2017)
• NASA JSC: ISO 5 certified cleanroom (Nov 2021); prohibited latex, nylon, polyamides, silicones; GN₂ (99.995%) purged storage in stainless steel/PTFE containers (Righter et al. 2023)
• Witness plates archived during ATLO; materials archive in ISO 7 cleanroom (Righter 2023)
• Procedural blanks: baked fused silica, sea sand, solvent blanks processed in parallel; Murchison meteorite analyzed alongside as positive control (Glavin 2025; Mojarro 2025)
• Comprehensive contamination knowledge program (Dworkin et al. 2026 preprint): most suspected contaminants traced to laboratory processes, not spacecraft or curation

Limitations:
• 1.24% of bulk sample escaped container and was contaminated with spacecraft particulates (Dworkin 2026)
• L-valine excess possibly from laboratory contamination (Glavin 2025)
• Ammonia measurement is a lower limit (hydrothermal treatment could release more from IOM) (Glavin 2025)
• Tryptophan detection tentative — trace signals only (Mojarro 2025)
• Some C6/C7 amino acids detected but not individually identified (Glavin 2025)

=== STARDUST / WILD 2 ===

Molecules Found:
• Glavin et al. 2008 (Meteorit Planet Sci, 2008): initial detection of suite of amino acids and amines (glycine, L-alanine, methylamine, ethylamine) in comet-exposed aerogel and foil
• Elsila et al. 2009 (Meteorit Planet Sci, 2009): isotopic confirmation that glycine is cometary; EACA identified as terrestrial Nylon-6 contaminant
• Altwegg et al. 2016 (Sci Adv, 2016): glycine + phosphorus detected in 67P coma by Rosetta/ROSINA, confirming Stardust results

Extraterrestrial Provenance Evidence:
• Glycine δ¹³C = +29 ± 6‰ vs terrestrial organic carbon range of −6 to −40‰ (Elsila 2009)
• Glycine detected only on aerogel-facing (comet-exposed) side of foils, not on backside (Elsila 2009)
• δ¹³C consistent with Murchison (+22 to +41‰) and Orgueil (+22‰) meteorites (Elsila 2009)
• EACA δ¹³C = −25 ± 2‰ matches JSC Nylon-6 bag material (−26.8 ± 0.2‰) — confirming terrestrial origin of that compound (Elsila 2009; Sandford 2010)

Contamination Controls:
• Commercial aluminum foil heated at 500°C overnight as procedural blank (Elsila 2009)
• Glassware heated at 500°C overnight (Elsila 2009)
• Aerogel witness coupon (WCARMI1CPN) analyzed for background amines (Sandford 2010)
• Spiked sample controls verified no isotopic fractionation during extraction (Elsila 2009)
• Isotopic matching of EACA to JSC Nylon-6 storage bags identified contamination source (Sandford 2010)

Limitations:
• Only glycine confirmed as cometary amino acid; β-alanine possibly cometary but insufficient material for isotopic analysis (Altwegg 2016)
• Measured glycine δ¹³C is a lower limit (may include terrestrial glycine from non-aerogel side) (Elsila 2009)
• EACA contamination from Nylon-6 bags well-characterized but indicates curation-era contamination (Sandford 2010)
• Limited sample quantity constrains analyses (Elsila 2009)

=== WHY MOLECULE DETECTION ≠ PROVENANCE ≠ BIOLOGICAL ORIGIN ===

  1. MOLECULE DETECTION: Simply identifying a compound via analytical techniques (GC-MS, LC-HRMS, etc.). E.g., detecting glycine in Stardust foils (Glavin 2008) or adenine in Bennu (Glavin 2025). Detection alone cannot distinguish extraterrestrial from terrestrial sources because these molecules are ubiquitous on Earth.

  2. EXTRATERRESTRIAL PROVENANCE: Establishing the molecule originated in the parent body environment, not on Earth. Requires positive evidence such as:

    • Isotopic signatures outside terrestrial ranges (δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N)
    • Racemic (non-enantiomERIC) mixtures for chiral molecules (biology produces homochiral L-amino acids)
    • Structural isomers rare/nonexistent in biology (6-methyluracil, isocytosine)
    • Distribution patterns violating biological rules (Chargaff's rule)
    • Absence in procedural blanks processed alongside samples
    • Spatial localization (glycine only on comet-exposed foil side)
      All three missions established provenance through combinations of these approaches.

  3. BIOLOGICAL ORIGIN: Requires evidence of life processes — metabolism, replication, enzymatic catalysis. None of these missions can establish biological origin. In fact, all findings point to ABOTIC synthesis: racemic mixtures prove non-biological formation; heavy isotopic enrichment reflects cold molecular cloud or parent-body chemistry, not biology; complex distributions of dozens of related compounds are hallmarks of abiotic aqueous alteration, not biosynthetic pathways. Finding life's building blocks demonstrates that prebiotic chemistry occurs throughout the Solar System — it does not constitute finding life.

=== KEY PAPER CITATIONS ===

  • Oba et al. 2023: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-36904-3
  • Koga et al. 2026: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-026-02791-z
  • Okazaki et al. 2017/2022: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abo7239
  • Yada et al. 2023: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40623-023-01924-2
  • Oba et al. 2026: https://www.nature.com/articles/s42004-026-01966-z

OSIRIS-REx:

  • Glavin et al. 2025: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-024-02472-9
  • Mojarro et al. 2025: https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2512461122
  • Dworkin et al. 2017: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6350808/
  • Righter et al. 2023: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/maps.13973
  • Dworkin et al. 2026: https://astrobiology.com/2026/09/15/osiris-rex-returned-a-pristine-sample-of-asteroid-bennu-takeaways-from-the-missions-contamination-control-and-knowledge-program/

evidence.snippet: 15 amino acids quantified + 5 tentatively identified in Ryugu A0106; chiral amino acids in approximately racemic mixtures (D/L ~ 1) indicating nonbiological origins; nonproteinogenic amino acids rare or nonexistent in terrestrial biology
evidence.supports: Hayabusa2/Ryugu: amino acid inventory and racemic mixture evidence for abiotic extraterrestrial origin

evidence.snippet: All five canonical nucleobases detected in Ryugu; δ13C = +25.5‰ to +33.9‰ and δ15N = +45.1‰ to +59.8‰ substantially enriched relative to terrestrial ranges; deviation from Chargaff's rule; structural isomers (6-methyluracil) support indigenous extraterrestrial origin; procedural blanks (baked sea sand, serpentine) showed absence/near-absence of peaks
evidence.supports: Hayabusa2/Ryugu: nucleobase detection with multiple independent lines of extraterrestrial provenance evidence

evidence.snippet: Bennu samples volatile-rich; 33 amino acids identified (14 of 20 proteinogenic); all five nucleobases; ammonia 13.6 μmol/g; δ15N = +180 ± 47‰ far outside terrestrial range; all chiral non-protein amino acids racemic; procedural blanks and Murchison comparison processed in parallel
evidence.supports: OSIRIS-REx/Bennu: comprehensive organic inventory with strong isotopic and chirality evidence for extraterrestrial provenance

evidence.snippet: TAGSAM head maintained at <180 ng/cm² amino acids and <180 ng/cm² hydrazine (achieved 0.96 ng/cm² amino acids); collection with high-purity N2/He gas; launch container under positive pressure purge; ISO 5 cleanroom design requirements
evidence.supports: OSIRIS-REx/Bennu: spacecraft-level contamination control strategy achieving unprecedented cleanliness

evidence.snippet: Glycine δ13C = +29 ± 6‰ strongly suggests extraterrestrial origin (terrestrial range −6 to −40‰); EACA δ13C = −25 ± 2‰ identical to JSC Nylon-6 bags (−26.8 ± 0.2‰) confirming terrestrial contamination; glycine detected only on aerogel-facing side; Al foil and glassware baked at 500°C as blanks
evidence.supports: Stardust/Wild 2: isotopic proof of cometary glycine and identification of Nylon-6 curation contamination

evidence.snippet: Comprehensive Stardust contamination assessment; EACA traced to Nylon-6 storage bags via isotopic matching; witness coupon analyzed; contamination sources documented for future sample return missions
evidence.supports: Stardust: systematic characterization of terrestrial contaminants enabling correction of analytical results

evidence.snippet: Hayabusa2 metal-seal system: softer Al alloy lid pressed onto harder Al alloy edge at ~2700 N; leak rate 1.9–2.3 Pa/hour; container pressure 68 Pa after 30 hours (vs ~5000 Pa for Hayabusa/Itokawa)
evidence.supports: Hayabusa2: metal-seal engineering enabling vacuum encapsulation of volatiles and organics

evidence.snippet: JAXA ESCuC: ISO 6 cleanroom; five serial clean chambers (vacuum to 10^-7 Pa; N2 with <200 ppb impurities); electrochemically polished SS304; <1 ng/cm² organic contamination; microbial testing negative
evidence.supports: Hayabusa2: ground-based curation facility achieving ultra-high cleanliness for sample handling
